## door v0.1.8 — keyboard-layout & battery indicators

Two small, opt-in status indicators for the greeter card. Both are **off by
default** — the built-in look is unchanged unless a theme turns them on — and both
are purely local reads: no daemon protocol, no network, no privileged path.

### Added
- **Keyboard-layout indicator** (`show_kb_layout`, default `false`) — a muted
  `⌨ US` row under the password field, so a login on an unexpected layout is
  visible instead of a silent auth failure. Reads the *configured* xkb layout
  locally, in order: `XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT`, then the localectl-managed
  `/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/00-keyboard.conf`, then `/etc/vconsole.conf` (primary
  layout of the list). It reports what the seat is set to — a Wayland client can't
  see a live per-keystroke switch, so the indicator names the configured layout,
  which is the thing that actually trips a login.
- **Battery indicator** (`show_battery`, default `false`) — a `⚡ 85%` row near the
  clock, from the first `/sys/class/power_supply/*` of type `Battery` (AC and USB
  supplies are skipped; `Charging`/`Full` shows the bolt). Hidden entirely on a
  machine with no battery, so a desktop asserts nothing.
- **door-settings** gains a toggle for each on the Behavior tab, with help text and
  a live-preview mock, plus documented keys in `greeter.toml`.

### Notes
- **Trust boundary unchanged.** Both indicators are unprivileged, local file reads
  in the greeter — no new greeter↔daemon message, and nothing touches the network
  (the `No network, ever` constraint holds).
- **Verified headless** on real hardware via `cage` + `grim`: a laptop run shows
  `⌨ US` + `⚡ 100%`; a desktop run (an empty `/sys/class/power_supply` presented to
  the greeter via a user+mount namespace) shows `⌨ US` with the battery row hidden,
  confirming the "no battery → assert nothing" path. Repro:
  `scripts/verify-indicators-desktop.sh`.
